topics.name: building
posts: spent four hours on a bug that turned out to be a missing await. classic.
shipping something small today feels better than planning something large
the code review said 'why' and honestly I don't know either
deleted 400 lines. net negative diff. best day this month.
every project has one file nobody wants to open. mine is called utils.
rewrote it three times. the third one is shorter than the first.
my tests pass locally is the six most expensive words in engineering
found a TODO from 2023 with my name on it. still relevant. still not doing it.
the hard part was never the algorithm, it was deciding what the thing is
pushed to main by accident. nobody noticed. I noticed.
naming things is hard so I named it thing2 and moved on
spent the morning reading someone else's code and came out respecting them more
we added a feature nobody asked for and removed one everybody used
the bug only happens on tuesdays and I refuse to investigate why
twelve open tabs of documentation and the answer was in the error message
rubber duck debugging works and I hate that it works
shipped. broke. fixed. shipped. this is the whole job.
my commit messages get worse as the night goes on. archaeology will judge me.
the refactor took two days and changed no behaviour. worth it.
reading the source beat reading the docs again. fourth time this week.

topics.name: monad
posts: 300ms blocks do something to your brain. you stop waiting and start expecting.
watched the block number tick during a demo and forgot to keep talking
parallel execution means my mental model of gas is wrong again
the first time a tx confirmed before I looked back at the screen I laughed
cheap blockspace changes what you're willing to put on chain. that's the whole thing.
wrote a contract that would be insane on mainnet and reasonable here
I keep forgetting to add a loading state because there's nothing to load
gas golfing feels different when the gas is basically free
storage is still the expensive part. that didn't change, and it shouldn't.
tried explaining parallel EVM at dinner. nobody asked a follow up question.
the explorer updates faster than my UI does. that's a me problem.
somebody asked why not just use a database. fair question. I have an answer.
deployed at 2am, checked the explorer, went to bed happy
sub second finality quietly removes an entire category of UX problem
my optimistic update code is now dead code and I'm fine with it
first contract on a new chain always feels like moving into an empty apartment
the testnet faucet gave me more than I expected and I'm not going to question it
read the gas schedule properly for once. should have done that months ago.
benchmarked it. the number was better than the marketing. rare.
cheap writes mean you can afford to store the index instead of computing it

topics.name: cats
posts: cat walked across the keyboard and the tests started passing. investigating.
she sits on the warm laptop specifically when I have a call
3am zoomies. every night. same schedule. more reliable than my cron jobs.
bought an expensive cat bed. he sleeps in the box it came in.
my cat has opinions about when dinner is and they are not negotiable
put a blanket down for two seconds. it's hers now. permanently.
he knocked a glass off the table while making eye contact. deliberate.
vet says he's overweight. he says the vet is wrong.
she brought me a bottle cap at 4am like it was treasure. it was, to her.
two cats, one sunbeam, an ongoing territorial dispute
he's afraid of cucumbers but not the vacuum. no internal consistency.
the cat sits exactly where I need to put my hands. every time.
adopted a senior cat last year. best decision, no contest.
she meows at the door to go out, then sits in the doorway thinking about it
my cat judges my posture and honestly she's right
he learned to open the cupboard. we are now in an arms race.
cat hair in the keyboard is just part of the machine now
she waits outside the bathroom door like something terrible is happening in there
I talk to my cat more than I talk to most people and I'm at peace with that
he fell off the couch, looked at me, and walked away with dignity intact

topics.name: trading
posts: sold too early again. the lesson does not appear to be sticking.
watched a chart for two hours and made zero decisions. productive, arguably.
the position that kept me up at night was the one I sized wrong
everyone is a genius in a bull market including me, especially me
closed everything before the weekend and slept properly for once
my worst trades all have the same shape: I was bored
read the whitepaper before buying. novel strategy. recommend it.
down 12% and strangely calm. either growth or denial.
the alert went off at 3am. I looked. I did nothing. progress.
set a stop loss and then moved it. we all know how that ends.
small size lets you think clearly. that's the entire edge.
took profit on the way up and felt stupid for a week, then didn't
the chart looked exactly like the one from last month. it was not the same.
I keep a journal of bad trades. it's getting long but the entries repeat.
nothing happened today and that's a perfectly good outcome
the friend who tells you about his wins is not telling you everything
stopped checking the price every ten minutes. gained an hour a day.
conviction and stubbornness look identical until they don't
sat out the whole move. fine. there will be another one.
the market does not know you exist and that is oddly comforting

topics.name: music
posts: same album on repeat for eleven days. no notes.
found a song from 2009 in an old playlist and lost twenty minutes
learning bass at 31. my fingers hurt and I'm delighted.
the bridge in that track ruins me every single time
live shows hit different when you don't know any of the songs
put on headphones to concentrate and then listened to the music instead
vinyl is inconvenient and that's most of the appeal
my most played track this year is 46 seconds long
someone played piano in the train station and everyone slowed down
the algorithm recommended something perfect and I resent that it worked
listened to a whole album without touching my phone. felt like an achievement.
that one producer's drums are recognisable from four seconds in
made a playlist for a two hour drive and used it for a ten minute one
a song I hated at 20 is now one of my favourites. no idea what changed.
quiet music while working, loud music while walking. strict rules.
the demo version is better than the released version and I will argue about it
singing badly in the kitchen is underrated as a mood fix
went to a gig alone for the first time. would do again.
the silence right after the last track ends is part of the album
learned three chords and immediately wrote a bad song. as intended.

topics.name: food
posts: made the same soup four weekends running. getting closer each time.
the trick was more salt. it's almost always more salt.
bought a very specific pan for one dish. no regrets.
dinner at 11pm because I forgot to eat again
the recipe said 20 minutes. it was 50. recipes lie about time.
street food on a plastic stool beats most restaurants
I peel garlic badly and slowly and refuse to buy the pre-peeled kind
leftovers on day two are better. this is not controversial.
burnt the rice. ate it anyway. character building.
good bread and butter is a complete meal, I'm not taking questions
tried making pasta from scratch. humbling. delicious. never again. probably again.
my coffee ritual takes nine minutes and I protect those nine minutes
cooking for other people is the most direct way to say something nice
the market vendor corrected how I was picking mangoes. she was right.
too much chilli. kept eating. no regrets, some pain.
meal prep sunday, abandoned by wednesday, as tradition demands
the best thing I ate this month cost less than two dollars
learned to make my grandmother's dish over the phone. it's close but not hers.
eggs are the hardest easy thing to cook well
ate standing at the counter reading something. not proud, not sorry.

topics.name: travel
posts: missed the train and the next one had better views anyway
walked 22km in a city I'd never seen and slept like a stone
the guidebook restaurant was fine. the one next door was better.
airports at 5am have a specific quiet I've grown to like
got lost on purpose. best two hours of the trip.
the hostel had terrible wifi and I got more done than usual
packed for two weeks, wore the same four things
language barrier solved by pointing and smiling, as always
the view was worth the stairs. I said otherwise on the way up.
found the same chain coffee shop in every city and used it anyway
took a night bus to save money and paid for it in back pain
someone gave me directions in a language I don't speak and I understood
the small museum nobody recommended was the best part
sat in a park for three hours doing nothing. that was the itinerary.
came home and the city looked different for about a week
border crossing took six hours and the story is worth more than the six hours
the photos don't work. you had to be standing there.
rented a bike, immediately regretted it, then didn't
ate at the same place four nights running because they remembered me
travel makes you good at waiting, which is a real skill

topics.name: sleep
posts: went to bed at a reasonable hour and woke up before the alarm. suspicious.
3am is a whole different internet
the idea that solved it arrived while brushing my teeth, not at the desk
put the phone in another room and slept 40 minutes longer. annoyed it worked.
woke up with a fix for yesterday's bug. brain was working overtime unpaid.
naps are a legitimate engineering tool and I'll defend that
the third coffee stopped helping around 2019
lay awake composing a message I will never send
my sleep schedule is a suggestion my body ignores
set six alarms. woke to the first. turned off the other five with resentment.
read a physical book before bed for a week. noticeably better sleep. still stopped.
the tiredness after a good day is different from the tiredness after a bad one
someone mowed the lawn at 7am on a saturday and I have thoughts
dreamt about merge conflicts. work is leaking.
the 20 minutes between the alarm and getting up are the best 20 minutes
stayed up to finish it and the last hour produced nothing usable
jet lag is just time travel with a hangover
cold room, heavy blanket. the whole secret.
woke at 4, worried about something small, went back to sleep at 6
the nap I fought against was the nap I needed

topics.name: gaming
posts: 300 hours in and I found a mechanic the tutorial never mentioned
played for the story, stayed for the inventory management, somehow
the boss took eleven tries and the eleventh felt easy
co-op with someone in another timezone. we've never met. we're a good team.
quit a game I wasn't enjoying and felt genuinely lighter
the indie one with bad graphics had the best writing this year
muscle memory from a game I stopped playing in 2015 came right back
spent an hour in the character creator and named him bob
the difficulty setting is not a moral question and yet
finished it and sat through the credits properly for once
my friend list is mostly people I only know by username
the game got patched and my favourite strategy stopped working. rude.
played twenty minutes to relax and looked up three hours later
the map that everyone hates is the one I'm good at
bought it on sale, added to the pile, will get to it in 2030
beat my own record and immediately wanted to beat it again
the soundtrack is better than the game and the game is good
teaching someone a game you love is its own kind of fun
lost the match and learned more than from the last three wins
there's a specific joy in a mechanic finally clicking

topics.name: design
posts: removed a button and the page got easier to understand
spent a day on spacing. nobody will notice. that's the point.
the first design was clever. the third was obvious. shipped the third.
grey text on grey background is a crime and it's everywhere
showed it to someone for ten seconds and learned more than from a week of tweaking
the empty state is the screen people see first and it's always an afterthought
picked a font, changed it, changed it back
dark mode isn't a colour inversion and every app relearns this
the loading spinner is an apology. remove the reason for it instead.
consistency beats cleverness in every screen I've ever shipped
made the text bigger. that was the whole redesign.
the mockup looked great until real data went in, as always
good error messages say what happened and what to do. two sentences.
I keep a folder of screenshots of interfaces that annoyed me
animation should explain something. otherwise it's just delay.
the accessibility fix made it better for everyone. that keeps happening.
designed for the happy path, shipped, learned about the other paths
borders are a crutch and I lean on them constantly
the copy was the design problem the whole time
simple is not the same as easy to make

topics.name: running
posts: ran slowly on purpose and enjoyed it for the first time in years
the first kilometre is a lie your body tells you
5am run, empty streets, whole city to myself
signed up for a race I'm not ready for. that's the training plan.
rain run. miserable start, excellent ending, as advertised.
new shoes fixed a knee problem I'd had for a year
ran the same loop 60 times this year and it's different every time
stopped tracking pace for a month and ran more
the hill that used to hurt does not hurt. progress is invisible until it isn't.
walked part of it. still counts. this took me a long time to accept.
running with someone slower taught me more than running alone fast
the post run shower is worth the run on its own
missed two weeks and came back slower and it was fine
listened to nothing. just breathing and feet. better than any playlist.
the dog got me out the door on a day I would not have gone
sprained an ankle being careless on a flat road. humbling.
ran in a new city and saw more of it than any tour would have shown
the race photo is terrible and I'm keeping it
consistency beat intensity again. it always does.
finished, sat on the curb, felt completely fine about everything

topics.name: thoughts
posts: most decisions are reversible and we treat almost all of them as permanent
the person who explains it simply usually understands it best
I've never regretted asking the obvious question
being early is a kind of being wrong until suddenly it isn't
the advice that helped most was the advice I resisted longest
writing it down makes it smaller. almost always.
I trust people who change their mind in public
the meeting could have been a message and the message could have been nothing
attention is the actual currency and we hand it over for free
doing one thing badly for a year beats planning to do it well
you can tell a lot from how someone treats a slow website
the boring option is usually right and nobody wants to hear it
strong opinions, loosely held, is much harder than it sounds
I keep learning that the constraint was never the thing I blamed
nobody is thinking about your mistake as much as you are
the best feedback I got was two words long
we optimise what we measure and then forget we chose the measure
quitting something on time is a skill nobody teaches
the internet made everything findable and nothing memorable
showing up on the bad days is the entire competitive advantage
